questions.question: Why should you avoid riding directly next to another vehicle?

options.text: The other driver may need your lane to pass.
You may be in the vehicle's blind spot.
You may lose access to escape routes.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be in the vehicle's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding next to another vehicle is dangerous because you could be in their blind spot. The driver won't see you there. Also, the vehicle may block your way to escape if a hazard appears.

questions.question: When should you do a pre-ride inspection?
questions.explanation: Small problems on a motorcycle are more dangerous than on a car. Check your motorcycle before every ride to stay safe.

questions.question: When is there less traction available for braking?

options.text: When a motorcycle is on dry pavement.

questions.explanation: When a motorcycle leans while turning, there is less grip for braking. You can still use both brakes while turning, but you must do it carefully.

questions.question: What should you look for in a protective motorcycle jacket?
questions.explanation: Choose a jacket made of leather or sturdy synthetic material. It should cover your arms completely, fit snugly, and allow movement. Jackets with built-in armor offer the best protection.

questions.question: What color are service signs?
questions.explanation: Blue signs with white letters show where services are located. These include rest areas, gas stations, food, and hospitals.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. This sign warns you that the road ahead will be slippery when wet.

questions.question: What should matter most when buying a motorcycle helmet?
questions.explanation: Protection is most important when choosing a helmet. Pick one that fastens securely, fits well, and is DOT-certified.

questions.question: Before riding, what should the throttle do when you release it?
questions.explanation: Check your throttle and clutch before riding. The throttle should snap back quickly when released. The clutch should feel tight and smooth.

questions.question: How should a motorcycle fit you?

options.text: Your fingertips should barely touch the handlebars when seated.
The seat should be one foot higher than your waist when standing next to it.
Your feet should comfortably touch the ground when seated.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your feet should comfortably touch the ground when seated.
questions.explanation: Your motorcycle fits correctly if your feet comfortably reach the ground while you sit on it. Make sure the fit is right before you ride.

questions.question: If you need to stop quickly, what should you do?

options.text: Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, apply steady pressure to both the front and rear brakes together. Be careful not to lock the brakes.

questions.question: You see an emergency vehicle stopped on the side of the road with flashing lights. What should you do?

options.text: Stop on the road behind the emergency vehicle.
Stop and wait until the emergency vehicle moves.
Move to a different lane away from the emergency vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to a different lane away from the emergency vehicle.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle, tow truck, or roadside assistance vehicle stopped with flashing lights, you must change lanes to give it extra space. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: When alcohol and drugs are used together, the effects are:

options.text: Less dangerous than using either one alone.
Often stronger than using either one alone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Often stronger than using either one alone.
questions.explanation: Many drugs, including prescription and over-the-counter medicines, can make it harder to ride safely. Some drugs become even more dangerous when mixed with alcohol.

questions.question: If a motorcycle rider takes a turn too fast, what may happen?

options.text: The rider will have better control of the motorcycle.
The ride will be more stable.
The motorcycle may leave the road by accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: The motorcycle may leave the road by accident.
questions.explanation: Taking a turn or curve too fast can cause a rider to lose control. The motorcycle may cross into another lane or go off the road.

questions.question: When traveling at night, judging distances is:

options.text: About the same as during the day.

questions.explanation: It is usually much harder to judge distances in the dark than in daylight. Shadows and light help you see how far away objects are. At night, artificial lights can distort or hide these natural clues.

questions.question: A good lane position should:

options.text: Help you see others and let them see you.
Place you in other drivers' blind spots.
Invite other drivers to share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help you see others and let them see you.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see others and lets them see you. It keeps you away from wind blasts, blind spots, and road hazards. It also stops other drivers from sharing your lane and gives you an escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: Taking over-the-counter medicine before riding:

options.text: Is usually safe because over-the-counter drugs are weak.
May hurt your riding skills and should be done carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: May hurt your riding skills and should be done carefully.
questions.explanation: Many drugs, including prescription and over-the-counter medicines, have side effects that can affect your riding. Always ask your doctor how a new medicine might affect your driving or riding.

questions.question: When riding, your feet should be:
questions.explanation: Keep your feet on the footrests while riding to help you stay balanced.

questions.question: If riding during the day, you should wear:

options.text: Brightly-colored clothes so other drivers can see you.
Any color clothes because other drivers can easily see you in daylight.
Dark clothes to stand out against the bright sun.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brightly-colored clothes so other drivers can see you.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen in daylight. Always wear bright colors to make yourself more visible, even during the day.

questions.question: You should check your motorcycle's safety before:
questions.explanation: Always check your motorcycle before you ride. Even small problems on a motorcycle can be more dangerous than small problems on a car.

questions.question: Riding gloves should be made of:
questions.explanation: Riding gloves should be made of leather or similar strong material for the best grip and protection.

questions.question: Which material protects you best in a crash?
questions.explanation: Leather and synthetic materials give riders the best protection during a crash. Always wear long pants and a jacket when riding.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign is on the back of slow-moving vehicles that travel below 25 mph, such as farm equipment or horse-drawn wagons.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, your lane position:

options.text: Has little effect on whether other drivers can see you.
Is very important because it affects whether other drivers can see you.
Cannot protect you from wind blasts from other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is very important because it affects whether other drivers can see you.
questions.explanation: Your lane position helps you see better and lets other drivers see you. Good positioning also protects you from wind blasts from other vehicles.

questions.question: You have a better chance of surviving a crash if you wear:
questions.explanation: A helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) standards gives the best head and neck protection. Wearing a good-quality, properly fitted helmet is the most important thing you can do to survive a crash.

questions.question: A DOT-approved helmet:

options.text: Lets you see as far to the sides as you need for safe riding.
Can become a hazard to the rider.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lets you see as far to the sides as you need for safe riding.
questions.explanation: Helmets do not limit your vision. Any DOT-approved helmet allows you to see as far as you need for safe riding.
